page.triggerNew.title: New trigger

page.triggers.intro: A trigger starts a pipeline by itself: on a schedule (cron), or when another system calls its webhook. It is bound to one version of a pipeline.
page.triggerNew.intro: Bind a schedule or a webhook to one version of a pipeline. Its runs are made as any run is, and are refused for the same reasons.
page.triggerEdit.intro: Change what the trigger runs, its schedule, its parameters or whether it is on. What is wrong is refused, and nothing changes.
triggers.col.name: Name
triggers.enabled.label: Enabled: {name}
triggers.empty.title: No triggers yet
triggers.empty.body: Make a trigger to run a pipeline on a schedule, or when another system calls it.
triggers.delete.title: Delete the trigger {name}?
triggers.delete.body: The trigger stops at once and its firing records are deleted with it. Runs it has already made stay. A webhook that is called with its secret gets 401 from then on.
triggerForm.name.help: Letters, digits, dot, underscore and hyphen; starts with a letter or digit. It is the name in the address of a webhook, and it cannot be changed later.
triggerForm.kind.webhook: Webhook: when another system calls it
triggerForm.target.ambiguous: More than one person uploaded this pipeline. Choose whose version you mean in the list; none is chosen for you.
triggerForm.target.help: One version of one pipeline. A new version of a jar is not run by the trigger until you change it here.
triggerForm.cron.help: Five fields: minute, hour, day of the month, month, day of the week.
triggerForm.cron.noPreview: There is no preview for this expression. The Engine checks it when you save.
triggerForm.cron.noPreview.fields: There is no preview: a cron expression has five fields (minute, hour, day of the month, month, day of the week). The Engine checks it when you save.
triggerForm.zone.help: An IANA time zone, such as Asia/Taipei. The expression is read in it; the Engine's default is UTC.
triggerForm.zone.browser: Use the time zone of this browser: {zone}
triggerForm.webhook.help: A webhook has no schedule. Its secret is shown once, when the trigger is made, and again only when you rotate it.
triggerForm.params.help: Only the parameters you fill in are given; the others get the default of the pipeline.
triggerForm.caller.label: Provided by the caller
triggerForm.caller.help: For a webhook, tick the parameters its caller gives in the body of each call. A parameter with a fixed value cannot also be ticked, and a ticked one has no fixed value.
triggerForm.caller.missing: {name} is required and has no default: give it a fixed value or tick “Provided by the caller”.
triggerForm.caller.both: {name} cannot have a fixed value and also be provided by the caller: clear the fixed value or untick the box.
error.problem.fixed_and_caller: {subject}: it has a fixed value and is also provided by the caller.
error.problem.caller_parameters_not_allo: Only a webhook trigger can have parameters provided by the caller.
triggerForm.enabled: On: it runs the pipeline when it is due or called
trigger.params.name: Name
trigger.secret.set: A secret is set, last changed:
trigger.secret.hidden: The secret is never shown again. If it is lost, rotate it to get a new one.
trigger.rotate.title: Rotate the secret of {name}?
trigger.rotate.body: A new secret is made and shown once. The old secret stops working at once: every system that calls this webhook with it gets 401 until it has the new one.
firing.runGone: The run was removed after the retention period.
firing.reason.unexpected_error: Something unexpected went wrong while the run was being made; the Engine's log has the cause.

allow.change.remove.title: Remove the entry {name}
allow.change.recheck.title: Judge every pipeline again
allow.trust: Adding an entry is a decision to trust. What a package or class on the list does inside is no longer checked, and a pipeline that refers to it is judged as if it were harmless.
allow.form.kind.package: Package: the package and its subpackages
allow.form.kind.class: Class: that class and its nested classes

allow.form.name.help.package: A package name, such as com.acme.util.
allow.form.name.help.class: A full class name with its package, such as com.acme.util.Strings. A class on the list still has its members that open files, networks or processes judged UNSAFE.
allow.form.exact: This package only, not its subpackages
allow.previewing: Working out the effect… The Engine reads every stored jar, which takes time when there are many.
allow.applying: Applying… The Engine judges every pipeline again in one step.
allow.preview.note: This is what would happen. Nothing has changed yet. The Engine judges again when you apply, so if someone changes the list meanwhile the result can differ.
allow.applied: The change is applied: version {version} is in force.
allow.applied.recheck: Every pipeline was judged again: version {version} is in force.
allow.impact.examined: Judged again: {definitions, plural, one {# pipeline} other {# pipelines}} in {artifacts, plural, one {# version} other {# versions}}.
allow.impact.revoked.warning.preview: {count, plural, one {# pipeline that may run although it is UNSAFE becomes UNSAFE again: that permission is taken back} other {# pipelines that may run although they are UNSAFE become UNSAFE: that permission is taken back}}. Runs of them are refused until an admin allows it again.
allow.impact.revoked.warning.applied: {count, plural, one {# pipeline lost its permission to run although it is UNSAFE: it was taken back} other {# pipelines lost their permission to run although they are UNSAFE: it was taken back}}. Runs of them are refused until an admin allows it again.
allow.impact.unreadable.note: A pipeline whose jar cannot be read again cannot be confirmed safe, so it is judged UNSAFE.
allow.impact.redundant: These entries are not needed any more; they are kept.
allow.limitations: What a verdict does not cover (the Engine's own words)
allow.refusal.exists: This entry exists already: {kind} {name}, added by {by}. To change it, change that entry.
allow.refusal.covered: The entry {kind} {name} already covers it, so it is not needed.
page.allowlist.intro: The packages and classes that a pipeline may refer to without being judged UNSAFE. Every change is previewed first, judges all stored pipelines again, and makes a new version.
allow.trust.note: An entry is a decision to trust: what a package or class on the list does inside is not checked any more. Preview the effect before you apply it.
allow.col.name: Name
allow.scope.class: the class and its nested classes
page.resources.intro: Shared resources limit how many runs may use something at once (a printer, an API with a quota). A pipeline declares the resources it needs; a run holds them while it runs and waits when they are all taken.
resources.empty.title: No shared resources yet
resources.empty.body: Define the resources that pipelines declare, so that runs of them can be made.
resources.overCapacity: More runs hold it than its capacity: the capacity was lowered, and the holders keep it until they end.
resources.waiters: Waiting for it, in the order they are served
resources.form.create.title: Define a shared resource
resources.form.change.title: Change {name}
resources.form.name: Name
resources.form.name.help: Letters, digits, dot, underscore and hyphen; starts with a letter or digit. It is the name that pipelines declare, and it cannot be changed later.
resources.form.capacity.help: How many runs may hold it at once. Lowering the capacity does not take the resource back from runs that hold it.
resources.form.capacity.invalid: The capacity must be a whole number of 1 or more.
resources.form.enabled.help: A disabled resource makes the runs that wait for it fail and refuses new runs that need it (409). The runs that hold it go on.
resources.form.waitersWarning: {count, plural, one {# run waits} other {# runs wait}} for this resource. Disabling it makes {count, plural, one {it} other {them}} fail.
resources.form.saveFail: Save and fail the waiting runs
resources.release.title: Make the run let go of {resource}?
resources.release.body: Run {run} of {pipeline} holds {resource}. It is not stopped: it goes on without holding the resource, so another run may use the resource at the same time as this one. Use this for a run that is stuck or forgotten.
error.not_a_holder: The run does not hold this resource (any more).
admin.title: Admin
admin.unsafe.title: Unsafe execution
admin.unsafe.label: Allow unsafe execution
admin.unsafe.help: Lets runs of this pipeline be made although the analysis judged it UNSAFE. The setting belongs to this version only and is not inherited: a new version of the jar starts as not allowed. A change of the allow-list that makes a SAFE pipeline UNSAFE takes the permission back.
admin.unsafe.safeNote: This pipeline is SAFE, so the setting has no effect now. It matters if a change of the allow-list makes it UNSAFE.
admin.unsafe.confirm.title: Allow {name} to run although it is UNSAFE?
admin.unsafe.confirm.body: Runs of this pipeline in version {hash} will be made although the analysis found {count, plural, one {# reason} other {# reasons}} against it. What the pipeline does is then not checked by the Engine: it can use the network and start processes as far as its declaration says, or more. Only allow what you trust.
admin.version.title: Version
admin.version.help: Removes this version of the jar and the pipelines in it. A version cannot be deleted while a trigger or a run that has not ended refers to it. Runs that have ended are deleted with it, after you have seen how many.
admin.version.confirm.title: Delete version {hash}?
admin.version.confirm.body: The version and {count, plural, one {its pipeline} other {its # pipelines}} will be removed, and no run can be made of {count, plural, one {it} other {them}} any more. This cannot be undone: to have it again, upload the same jar.
secretStatus.invalid_secret: In the keystore, but not usable: not printable ASCII
checkFailure.root_unavailable: the resource root is missing or cannot be read and written
checkFailure.parent_not_creatable: the directory of the file is missing and cannot be made
checkFailure.not_readable_writable: the file cannot be read and written
checkFailure.path_outside_root: the path leads out of the resource root
checkFailure.connection_failed: the service could not be reached
checkFailure.server_error: the service answered with a server error
checkFailure.unexpected_response: the service answered, but not as a check expects
checkFailure.redirect_blocked: the service sent the check outside its address
checkFailure.alias_missing: the secret alias is not in the keystore (nothing was sent)
checkFailure.alias_invalid: the secret in the keystore cannot be used (nothing was sent)
checkFailure.error: the check itself went wrong; the Engine log has the details
resources.declaredBy.summary: Used by {count, plural, one {# pipeline definition} other {# pipeline definitions}} through their roles, with {triggers, plural, one {# trigger} other {# triggers}} bound to them
resources.delete.title: Delete {name}?
resources.delete.declared: {definitions, plural, =0 {No pipeline definition uses it} one {# pipeline definition uses it} other {# pipeline definitions use it}}, with {triggers, plural, one {# trigger} other {# triggers}} bound to {definitions, plural, one {it} other {them}}.
resources.delete.free: No run holds it or waits for it.
resources.delete.used: {holders, plural, one {# run holds it} other {# runs hold it}} and {waiters, plural, one {# run waits for it} other {# runs wait for it}}.
resources.delete.body: The pipelines keep their declaration: from now on, runs of them (by hand or by their triggers) are refused, as for a resource that was never defined, until a resource of this name is defined again (of any type). The Engine logs who deleted it.
resources.delete.inUse: It cannot be deleted while it is in use: {holders, plural, one {# run holds it} other {# runs hold it}} and {waiters, plural, one {# run waits for it} other {# runs wait for it}}.
resources.delete.inUse.how: To free it, disable it (the runs that wait for it fail) and wait for the holders to end, or release the holders on its card; then delete it.
secrets.title: Keystore secrets
secrets.intro: The secrets that resources use (keys of services, database passwords) are only in the Engine's keystore, which it opens read-only. The Console and the API never show a secret's value and never take one: to add or change a secret, an operator changes the keystore with keytool (see the keystore runbook) and then reloads it here. Resources refer to a secret by its alias.
secrets.notWebhook: These are not the secrets of webhook triggers: a webhook secret is made by the Engine and shown once, when the trigger is made or its secret is rotated.
secrets.notConfigured: The Engine has no keystore configured, so there are no secrets to show or reload. An operator configures one with RUNLINE_KEYSTORE_PATH and its password when the Engine starts.
secrets.reloaded: Reloaded: the keystore has {aliases, plural, one {# alias} other {# aliases}}.
secrets.reloaded.none: No alias changed since the last reload.
secrets.reloaded.changed: Added, removed or changed: runs that take these resources from now on use the new secrets; runs that hold them now keep the old ones.
error.problem.corrupt: The keystore file is damaged or cut short.
error.problem.wrong_format: The keystore file is not PKCS12.
error.problem.unreadable: The keystore file could not be opened.
resources.form.type.help: What the resource is. A counter only limits how many runs hold it at once. The type cannot be changed later: to change it, delete the resource and define it again.
resources.form.fixed: The name and the type cannot be changed: to change them, delete the resource and define it again.
warning.resource_type_mismatch: The shared resource {resource} is not of the type the pipeline declares: no run can be created until the two agree, or another shared resource is chosen for the role.
warning.resource_type_unknown: The type declared for the shared resource {resource} is not one the Engine knows: runs are refused as for a type that does not match.
resources.form.secret.jdbc-pool: Password of the account: its alias in the keystore
resources.form.secret.openai-compatible: API key: its alias in the keystore
resources.form.secret.notConfigured: The Engine has no keystore, so there is no secret to choose.
resources.form.secret.empty: The keystore has no secret to choose (certificates are not secrets).
resources.form.secret.help: The Console never takes a secret value: operators add and replace secrets in the keystore with keytool, then reload it on this page. Once a resource has an alias it can be changed to another, not removed.
resources.form.pair.name: Name
resources.form.path.help: Relative to the resource root of the Engine (RUNLINE_RESOURCE_ROOT); its directory is made when needed. An absolute path, or one that leads out of the resource root, is refused.
resources.form.jdbc.username.help: Use an account of its own with the least rights the pipelines need: what a pipeline can do is what this account can do. Its password is the alias chosen below.
resources.form.jdbc.path.help: The file of the database, relative to the resource root of the Engine (for example runs/digest.db). It is made when a run first needs it, in a directory that must already be there. There is no account or password.
resources.form.jdbc.properties.help: Only what the Engine allows for the kind of database (listed below). Never a password or an address.
resources.form.jdbc.pool: Pool size = capacity × connections per run = {capacity} × {perRun} = {size}. The pool cannot be sized on its own; a run keeps the connections it used until it ends.
resources.form.timeouts.help: Empty: the Engine's default, shown in grey.
resources.form.timeout.quotaWaitMs: Wait for a share of the run
resources.form.openai.baseUrl.help: http or https, with the root path of the API (e.g. /v1). Pipelines cannot choose another host, path or header.
resources.form.openai.headers.help: Sent with every request; not secret. A name that looks like a credential (auth, key, token, secret, cookie) or a header the Engine sets is refused: the key is the alias chosen below. The organization and project are sent as OpenAI-Organization and OpenAI-Project.
resources.form.openai.endpoints.help: Pipelines can call only these entries of the Engine's catalog, under the address. A new resource has the entries marked for it; enable the others one by one or by group, above all those that change what the service keeps.
resources.form.openai.parameters.help: A default is used when the pipeline does not give the parameter; the pipeline's own value replaces it. A locked parameter cannot be given by the pipeline at all: a call that gives it is refused, and the default (if any) is what is sent. A ceiling is the highest number a pipeline may give; a call above it is refused. Defaults must keep to the allowed models and the ceilings.
resources.form.openai.allowedModels.help: Separated by commas; empty for any. When there are some, a request without a model (and without a default model) is refused too.
resources.form.openai.timeouts.help: Empty: the Engine's default, shown in grey; the whole call has none unless one is set. First byte covers the generation of a call that is not streamed.
resources.form.openai.limit: Requests to the service at once, at most = capacity × requests per run = {capacity} × {perRun} = {limit}.
resources.problem.name: The name is not valid: letters, digits, dot, underscore and hyphen, starting with a letter or digit.
resources.problem.capacity: The capacity must be 1 or more.
resources.problem.invalid_secret_alias: This type has no secret, or the alias is not valid.
resources.problem.path_outside_root: The path leads outside the resource root: an absolute path, .. or a link out of it.
resources.problem.path_unusable: The path cannot be used now: the resource root is unusable, its directory cannot be made, or the file cannot be read and written.
resources.problem.invalid_settings: The settings are not valid for this type.
resources.problem.invalid_settings.jdbc-: The Engine refused the host, port, database name or account: a host is a name or an address without a port, slash or space; a database name has letters, digits, _ . $ -; a port is 1 to 65535.
resources.problem.invalid_settings.opena: The Engine refused the settings: the address is missing, or the organization or project is empty.
resources.problem.unsupported_database: The Engine has no profile for this kind of database.
resources.problem.property_not_allowed: A property is not allowed for this database: only its allowed properties, never one that loads classes, writes files, carries a secret, reaches elsewhere or has to do with TLS.
resources.problem.invalid_base_url: Not an http or https address of its own: no user, query, fragment, . or .. in it.
resources.problem.invalid_header: A header, the organization or the project is not allowed: a name that looks like a credential (auth, key, token, secret, cookie), a header the Engine sets, or a value with a line break.
resources.problem.invalid_endpoint: An endpoint is not in the Engine's catalog, or none is enabled.
resources.problem.invalid_request_defaul: The parameters are not valid: a default of the wrong kind, a lock or ceiling of a parameter that cannot have one, or a default against the allowed models or a ceiling.
resources.problem.invalid_timeout: A timeout is not a whole number of milliseconds from 1 to a day.
resources.problem.invalid_limit: A limit is out of its range.
resources.problem.invalid_limit.jdbc-poo: Connections per run go from 1 to 64.
resources.problem.invalid_limit.openai-c: Requests per run go from 1 to 256.
resources.use.activeConnections: Connections in use: {count, number} of {limit, number}
resources.use.inFlightRequests: Requests in flight: {count, number} of {limit, number}
secretStatus.wrong_type: In the keystore, but not a secret
keystoreStatus.invalid_key: Not usable: the keystore's password does not open the key
secrets.certificate.daysLeft: {days, plural, one {# day left} other {# days left}}
secrets.certificate.expiring: Expires soon: renew it in the keystore and reload
resources.form.certificates.title: Certificates (TLS)
resources.form.certificates.help.jdbc-po: With a trusted certificate or a client certificate, the connection always uses TLS and verifies the certificate and the host name (sslmode verify-full); with trusted certificates, only they are trusted. With neither, the connection is as the database driver makes it by default.
resources.form.certificates.help.openai-: For an https address only. With trusted certificates, only they are trusted, not the JVM's default; without, the JVM's default trust is used. The host name is always verified.
resources.form.certificates.client: Client certificate (mTLS): a private key entry
resources.form.certificates.noTrusted: The keystore has no trusted certificate to choose.
resources.form.certificates.daysLeft: {days, plural, one {# day left} other {# days left}}
resources.form.certificates.unusableKey: {alias} (not usable: the keystore's password does not open it)
resources.form.certificates.notConfigure: The Engine has no keystore, so there is no certificate to choose.
resources.form.certificates.keytool: Operators add and replace certificates in the keystore with keytool, then reload it on this page. Nothing of a private key is ever shown.
resources.problem.alias_wrong_type: An alias names an entry of another kind: a secret only for the secret, trusted certificates only for trust, a private key only for the client certificate.
checkFailure.alias_wrong_type: an alias names an entry of another kind in the keystore (nothing was sent)
checkFailure.trust_failed: the service's certificate is not one the resource trusts
checkFailure.hostname_mismatch: the service's certificate is not for this host
checkFailure.client_cert_rejected: the service asked for a client certificate and refused the connection
resources.catalog.failed: The Engine's resource types could not be read, so database pools and OpenAI-compatible services can be neither defined nor changed here now. Open the page again to retry; counters and files are not affected.
resources.form.catalogUnavailable: The Engine's resource types could not be read, so this resource cannot be changed now. Open the page again to retry.
resources.form.jdbc.properties.none: This kind of database allows no extra property.
bindings.intro: Choose which shared resource each role of this pipeline uses. A role you have not chosen for uses the shared resource of the same name, if there is one. What you choose applies to every version of this pipeline that you upload.
bindings.uploader.help: Each uploader has bindings of their own for a pipeline of this name. These are the bindings of the one chosen here.
bindings.current.default: Not bound. It uses the shared resource of the same name, {resource} (the default).
bindings.current.none: Not bound, and no shared resource is named {resource}.
bindings.problem.unbound: No run of this pipeline can be created until a shared resource is chosen for this role.
bindings.problem.unknown: {resource} is bound to this role but is not defined (it may have been deleted). No run of this pipeline can be created until another shared resource is chosen.
bindings.problem.disabled: {resource} is disabled. No run of this pipeline can be created until it is enabled or another shared resource is chosen.
bindings.problem.type_mismatch: {resource} is not of the type this role needs. No run of this pipeline can be created until a shared resource of that type is chosen.
bindings.problem.other: {resource} cannot be used by this role. No run of this pipeline can be created until that is settled.
bindings.cannotRun: No run of this pipeline can be created yet. These roles need a shared resource first:
bindings.choose.none: No shared resource of this type exists.
bindings.choose.define: Define one on the Resources page
bindings.choose.askAdmin: Ask an administrator to define one.
bindings.stale.title: Bindings of roles this version does not declare
bindings.stale.help: They do not affect this version. You can remove them.
createRun.unavailable: A run needs a shared resource for each of these roles. Choose one, then create the run again:
page.users.title: Users
page.users.intro: The people who have signed in with the login service. Disabling a person ends all of their sessions at once and refuses their sign-in until you enable them again; nothing changes at the login service. Tokens from API_TOKENS are not people who sign in: they are not listed and are not affected.
users.col.name: Name
users.empty.title: Nobody has signed in yet
users.empty.body: People appear here after their first sign-in with the login service.
users.disable.title: Disable {name}?
users.disable.body: {name} is signed out of every session at once: their next request is refused and they are sent back to the sign-in. They cannot sign in again until you enable them.
users.disable.self: This is your own account: you will be signed out too. A token from API_TOKENS still gets you back in.
users.enable.title: Enable {name}?
users.enable.body: {name} can sign in again. The sessions that ended do not come back.
users.result.disabled: Disabled {name}. {count, plural, one {# session ended.} other {# sessions ended.}}
users.result.sessionsEnded: Ended {count, plural, one {# session} other {# sessions}} of {name}.
users.sessions.title: Sessions of {name}
users.sessions.endAll.title: End all sessions of {name}?
users.sessions.endAll.body: Every session of {name} ends now: they are sent back to the sign-in on their next request. They are not disabled and can sign in again.
views.title: Data
views.intro: Tables the pipeline keeps in its own database. They can be read here and not changed.
views.problem.unbound: The role {role} has no shared resource: none is bound to it, and none has its name.
views.problem.unknown: The shared resource bound to the role {role} is not defined (it may have been deleted).
views.problem.disabled: The shared resource of the role {role} is disabled.
views.problem.type_mismatch: The shared resource of the role {role} is not of the type the pipeline expects.
views.invalid.not_an_option: {parameter} must be one of the listed values.
views.invalid.unknown: {parameter} is not a parameter of this view.
views.hint.view_timeout: Narrow the table with the values above, or try again in a moment.
views.hint.view_busy: Wait a moment and try again.
views.hint.view_connection_failed: Try again. If it keeps failing, ask an administrator to check the shared resource.
views.hint.view_schema_mismatch: If the pipeline was upgraded, the tables appear after its next run. Try again once a run has finished.
views.hint.view_query_rejected: This is a problem in the view the pipeline declares. Tell the person who wrote the pipeline.
views.hint.view_result_too_large: Narrow the table with the values above, or tell the person who wrote the pipeline.
views.hint.view_resource_unavailable: Settle the shared resource of the role, then try again.
views.hint.invalid_view_parameter: Change the values above and show the table again.
views.hint.view_not_found: Go back to the list of views.
views.hint.other: Try again. If it keeps failing, give the error ID to an administrator.
error.view_not_found: This pipeline version declares no such view.
error.view_resource_unavailable: The database this view reads cannot be used right now.
error.view_resource_unavailable.unbound: No shared resource is bound to the role the view reads, and none has its name.
error.view_resource_unavailable.unknown: The shared resource bound to the role the view reads is not defined (it may have been deleted).
error.view_resource_unavailable.disabled: The shared resource of the role the view reads is disabled.
error.view_resource_unavailable.type_mis: The shared resource of the role the view reads is not of the type the pipeline expects.
error.view_schema_mismatch: The tables this view reads are not in the database.
error.view_query_rejected: The database did not accept the query of this view.
error.view_result_too_large: This page of the view is too large to show.
error.view_busy: The database is busy reading other views.
error.view_connection_failed: The database cannot be reached, or it does not accept the account.
error.view_timeout: The database took too long to answer, so the read was cancelled.
error.view_declaration_invalid: A view the pipeline declares is not valid, so the jar was not accepted.
error.invalid_view_parameter: A value for this view is not valid.
admin.version.blocked.triggers: Delete the trigger, or bind it to another version, first. Triggers bound to this version:
admin.version.blocked.active: {count, plural, one {# run has} other {# runs have}} not ended. Cancel {count, plural, one {it} other {them}} or wait until {count, plural, one {it ends} other {they end}}, then try again.
admin.version.impact.logs: {count, plural, one {# log entry} other {# log entries}}
admin.version.impact.jarRemoved: The jar is removed too, because no other version has this content.
admin.version.impact.jarStays: The jar stays, because another version has the same content.
admin.version.effect.withRuns: The runs and their log entries will be deleted with the version and cannot be recovered.
admin.version.effect.noRuns: This version has no runs. Only the version is deleted.
